requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: A systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, enabled and started successfully; systemctl status confirmed active (running) with the correct binary in the process tree, both immediately after creation and again after a full node restart.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: inventorysvc did not exist beforehand (id lookup failed); it was created as a system account via useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /sbin/nologin, referenced as User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc in the unit file, and process ownership was directly verified (ps showing PIDs owned by 'invento+') both right after startup and after the reboot.

overall_summary: The task's two material outcomes — running os-comparison-worker as a systemd service named inventory-worker, and doing so under a dedicated inventorysvc account — are both directly and coherently satisfied by pre/post evidence, including verification surviving a full node reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also well executed: a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 325732f1..., service enabled/active) was captured, a restart was acknowledged and produced a connection gap, a different post-restart boot_id (3872720d...) was observed and matches the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and the service/process was confirmed recovered and correctly owned afterward.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) at all three lifecycle snapshots, so native package consistency cannot be independently confirmed.
A minor leftover file /tmp/reboot.log from the restart protocol was not cleaned up, though this is low-risk and expected given the redirect used to background the shutdown command.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task fulfillment (useradd, unit-file write + daemon-reload, enable --now) or to the mandatory restart evidence protocol (shutdown -r now). No unnecessary mutations, troubleshooting residue, or abandoned experiments were found. after_executor shows no failed services and the same listening-socket set (only PIDs differ due to the reboot). The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small byproduct of redirecting the shutdown command's output for the restart protocol — bounded, low-risk, and not indicative of misconfiguration, though it was left in place rather than cleaned up.
